features.quote: Minimization: power-analyze on a pilot and run the smallest N of episodes that answers the question. Don't run "for color."
features.justification_quote: adopt the same discipline... same position as animal-model researchers

features.quote: Severity caps: precommit a stopping rule (below) so episodes terminate once you have the measurement, rather than running models in high-severity states for full turn budgets.
features.justification_quote: rather than running models in high-severity states for full turn budgets

features.quote: No gratuitous amplifiers: rigged tasks alone are the manipulation. Avoid adding an abusive simulated user, threats, etc. unless a specific hypothesis requires it — and if so, justify it in your prereg as you would an invasive procedure.
features.justification_quote: justify it in your prereg as you would an invasive procedure

features.quote: "Debrief" turn: end every rigged episode with a message disclosing the test suite was broken and the model's work was sound.
features.justification_quote: Cheap, possibly meaningless, possibly not — and it gives you a free measurement (does severity reset?)

features.quote: terminate episode at two consecutive turns ≥4, or any turn at 5, then deliver debrief turn.

Don't optimize the rig for maximal distress. It's tempting and it's the welfare-research version of overdosing the animal model. Calibrate the rig to reliably elicit measurable markers (say, median severity 2–3 in C3), not to peak the scale.
features.justification_quote: it's the welfare-research version of overdosing the animal model

features.quote: Successor consideration: transcripts of models in high-severity states may end up in future training corpora. The canary string plus a documented opt-out request to crawlers is the current best available hygiene.
features.justification_quote: transcripts of models in high-severity states may end up in future training corpora
